newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries dip in London, eye FOMC later.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries dip in London, eye FOMC later.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were a touch lower in London on Tuesday with activity confined to a handful of players juggling positions ahead of a key U.S. interest rate decision later.

The market's ominously quiet tone could change just before the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meets as players may engage in last-minute position shifting, traders said. A decision is expected around 1815 GMT.
But trade in the London time zone was likely to stay thin.
"The bets are all on anyway," said one trader.
By 1028 GMT, the 30-year T-bond was at 96-10 to yield 6.92 percent, unchanged from Tokyo and up from 96-09 at the New York close.
The dollar's steep fall against the yen overnight to five-month lows below 112 had limited impact on Treasuries, dealers said. By European mid-morning, the dollar was recovering ground above 113 yen.
"There are arguments that there may be sellers who are already long (of Treasuries), but they've probably lost quite a bit of money on it already," said the London trader.
The long term effect on Treasuries from a weaker dollar/yen was also likely to be limited as Japanese investors weren't big holders of U.S. bonds, analysts said.
"The direction will come from what the Fed does rather than what the currencies have done," said the trader.

Adrian Schmidt, senior economist at Chase in London, said the ease in Treasuries reflected a slight shift among players towards the camp forecasting a rate hike in the federal funds rate, currently at 5.50 percent.
"I think they are just adjusting to what they thought was maybe a slightly overly bullish attitude towards it," Schmidt said.
The market would jolt one way or another after the rate announcement, but not much as the dollar's moves and expectation of a hike in July if the Fed holds fire this time, would cap the impact.
"A rise at this stage will be seen as an insurance policy move. In practice I don't think you would see much more than a half a point decline in the long end," said Schmidt.
By 1039 GMT, the June T-bond future traded at 109-29 in automated trade, unchanged from Chicago's close on Monday. --Clelia Oziel, International Bonds Unit +44-171-542 8663
